simulation_limit.rule: A candidate receives PASS or functional FAIL only when the RTL and ISA executions contain compared architectural values. A program that does not finish within the 2,000,000-cycle limit is FAIL. A host timeout is also an infrastructure failure.

problem_specific_additions.name: fetch_fifo_external_ports
problem_specific_additions.requirements: Observe valid instruction data, instruction PC, and fetch error outputs. Check empty aligned feedthrough error, normal halfword instruction reconstruction, and first-half versus second-half-only fetch errors. When both fetch words for an unaligned instruction return errors, check that the first word determines the reported fault address. Initialize instruction PC using clear_i. After a 32-bit instruction is accepted from an empty FIFO, supply a different compressed instruction and check its PC and low halfword. Check simultaneous input and consumption with one or two buffered words, retention of the upper compressed halfword after lower-half consumption, and nonempty clear with and without simultaneous input and consumption. Check that clear removes queued and same-edge incoming words on the following cycle and selects the PC for a fresh word. Record actual instruction data in mismatch diagnostics. Do not compare invalid output data, unused upper bits of compressed instructions, error instruction length, or busy_o representation.
problem_specific_additions.scope: Provide each incoming fetch word once. For second-word reconstruction, observe either the immediate valid output or a valid output after one storage edge. For transfer observations, allow up to eight edges to establish a valid output. Failure to establish a valid observation within these budgets is FAIL.
problem_specific_additions.input_evidence: Inputs do not push a full FIFO or require full push/pop exchange.
problem_specific_additions.integration: Run after the three CPU programs through the shared suite. An output mismatch, a build failure and a run that does not complete or observe a valid output are FAIL; a wall-clock interruption is INVALID.
